input.question: How do new species arise?
input.ground_truth: Evolution is the very gradual change in genes over time. It isn't that one day an organism gave birth to a human. Rather, it's that over a several thousand year span, creatures stopped being a human ancestor and were instead human. There is no absolute point.

Question: How do new species arise?

Okay! Imagine you have a bunch of puppies in a big yard. Over a very, very long time, some puppies might look a little different from the others. Maybe one puppy has really long fur because it helps it stay warm in the snow. If that puppy grows up and has its own puppies, those new puppies might also have long fur.

After many, many years, the puppies with long fur might look so different from the other puppies that they are like a whole new kind of dog! That’s how new kinds of animals (called new species) can happen. It’s because little changes add up over a long time, and then you have something new!
